candidates.name: Fetal akinesia deformation sequence
support_spans: microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
candidates.why: The presence of microcephaly and ventricular enlargement in the fetal ultrasound, along with the postnatal MRI findings, suggests a condition that affects fetal development.

candidates.name: Hydrocephalus
support_spans: marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles
contradict_spans: without signs of elevated intracranial pressure
candidates.why: The marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles is a key feature of hydrocephalus, but the absence of elevated intracranial pressure is an important consideration.

candidates.name: Leber congenital amaurosis
support_spans: very weak light reflexes bilaterally
mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign
candidates.why: The weak light reflexes and optic nerve pallor, along with the peripapillary double-ring sign, are consistent with Leber congenital amaurosis, a condition that affects the retina and causes severe visual impairment.

key_evidence_spans: marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure
mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign

candidates.name: Fetal Twin Transfusion Syndrome with Brain Injury
support_spans: one of monochorionic diamniotic twins; her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
candidates.why: The presence of monochorionic diamniotic twins and the death of one twin in utero suggests a possible fetal twin transfusion syndrome, which could have led to brain injury and the observed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement.
candidates.protected_reason: This condition may be easily missed due to its rarity and the complexity of its presentation.

candidates.name: Congenital Infection
support_spans: microcephaly
ventricular enlargement
candidates.why: The presence of microcephaly and ventricular enlargement could suggest a congenital infection, although the noncontributory family history makes this less likely.
candidates.protected_reason: Congenital infections can have a wide range of presentations and may be overlooked if not specifically considered.

candidates.name: Walker-Warburg Syndrome
support_spans: microcephaly
marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles
severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
contradict_spans: the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
candidates.why: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and lobar thinning is suggestive of Walker-Warburg Syndrome, although the preservation of certain brain structures is not typical of this condition.
candidates.protected_reason: Walker-Warburg Syndrome is a rare condition that may be overlooked due to its low prevalence and variable presentation.
